election.name: November 4, 2025 Lakewood city election (coordinated election)
election.summary: Lakewood voters chose City Council members in all five wards; four incumbents were reelected and Liz Black won the open Ward 2 seat. Voters also chose three Jeffco Public Schools board members and decided two statewide measures, Propositions LL and MM, which both passed. There were no City of Lakewood ballot questions.
election.turnout: In Lakewood's five wards, 45,817 ballots were cast out of 112,168 registered voters (about 40.85%, summed from county ward totals). Jefferson County overall: 199,921 of 440,729 (45.36%). Statewide: 1,716,655 of 4,135,705 active voters (41.51%).

measures.short_title: Keep revenue already collected for Healthy School Meals for All
measures.summary: Asked whether the state could keep and spend money it had collected above estimates from the 2022 voter-approved limits on income tax deductions for people with incomes of $300,000 or more, and keep those limits in place, to fund the free school meals program. Totals shown are statewide certified results.

measures.short_title: Further limit income tax deductions for high earners to fund school meals and food aid
measures.summary: Asked whether to raise about $95 million a year by limiting state income tax deductions to $1,000 for single filers or $2,000 for joint filers with federal taxable income of $300,000 or more. The money goes to the school meals program, wages for school food workers, and SNAP food assistance. Totals shown are statewide certified results.

facts.text: There were no City of Lakewood ballot questions, no Jefferson County measures, and no Jeffco Public Schools measures on the November 2025 ballot. The special-district measures on the county ballot (Lookout Mountain Water, Mountain Shadows Metro, South Metro Fire Rescue, Coal Creek Canyon Fire) were for other areas.

Lakewood holds regular city elections in November of odd-numbered years. The mayor and council members serve four-year terms. The mayor was not on the 2025 ballot; Mayor Wendi Strom's term runs November 2023 to November 2027.
Adding the five ward totals in the county's statement of votes cast: 45,817 ballots were cast in Lakewood's wards out of 112,168 registered voters (about 40.85%).

Jefferson County: 199,921 ballots cast out of 440,729 registered voters (45.36%). The Clerk reports 196,849 voted by mail and 2,979 in person. The county canvass certified results on November 25, 2025.
Statewide, 1,716,655 ballots were cast out of 4,135,705 active voters (41.51%). The Secretary of State certified results on November 26, 2025.
New and reelected council members were sworn in on November 24, 2025: Jeslin Shahrezaei, Liz Black, Ken Cruz, Bill Furman and Paula Nystrom.
The three newly elected Jeffco school board members (Echevarria, Gibbins, Moeinian) were scheduled to be sworn in on December 3, 2025, to four-year terms.

On October 13, 2025, the City Council gave final approval to a nearly 400-page zoning code update, made up of four ordinances (2025-27, 2025-28, 2025-29 and 2025-30). The new rules replaced single-family-only zones with residential zones that allow more than one home per lot. Residents then petitioned to refer all four ordinances to voters, which led to the April 7, 2026 special election.

open_questions: Lakewood council results come from Jefferson County's Statement of Votes Cast run on Nov. 20, 2025 (before the Nov. 25 canvass certification) and linked as the 2025 results record; the PDF is not labeled certified. Confirm against the certified Clarity results (results.enr.clarityelections.com/CO/Jefferson/124410/), which could not be fetched.
Certified Jeffco Public Schools board vote totals were not retrieved (the county PDF text was cut off at page 72 of 182 and the Clarity site could not be fetched). Board counts shown are preliminary.
Jefferson County totals for Propositions LL and MM were not retrieved; only statewide certified totals are shown.

The City of Lakewood's 2025 election page lists a different candidate set (Ward 1: Robert James Hooser; Ward 2: Alexei Fernandez; Ward 4: Nicholas Munden as a listed candidate) than the county ballot results. These names did not appear on the county results as ballot candidates (Munden was a qualified write-in); the city page may be an early or outdated list.
Party affiliation is not listed because Lakewood council and Jeffco school board races are nonpartisan.

Exact council vote counts and dates of each reading for ordinances 2025-27 to 2025-30 were not confirmed; a city legal notice for O-2025-28 showed a planned final passage of Sept. 8, 2025, while news reports say the full update received final approval Oct. 13, 2025.
